unit.title: Clean floors, walls, furniture and furnishings

summary: This unit teaches you to clean the hard surfaces and fittings of a villa, hotel or guest house safely and to a guest-ready standard. You will learn to identify each surface, choose the right cleaning product and equipment, clean floors by hand and with a rotary floor machine, wash walls, dust and polish furniture, care for glass, metal, lamps, blinds and other furnishings, work safely at height, deal with Jamaica's damp, salty and sandy conditions, and check and report your work.

blocks.p: A villa or hotel is only as clean as its floors, walls and furniture look and smell. Guests notice a dull floor, a dusty picture frame or a sticky table straight away. But cleaning is also a skill: the wrong cleaner, too much water or the wrong pad can ruin a marble floor, lift the boards of a wooden floor or strip the paint from a wall. This unit teaches you to **know the surface before you clean it**.

This unit is for HOSPITALITY VILLA/PROPERTIES SERVICES LEVEL 2 trainees who will clean guest rooms, living areas, corridors and terraces. You will use hand tools and, with training and permission, a rotary floor machine, a wet-and-dry vacuum and a stepladder.

blocks.note: How you are assessed: theory papers (multiple-choice questions, short answers and essays) and group practical tasks in the Centre's training room or mock villa: scrubbing and polishing a hard floor with a rotary floor machine, and cleaning the walls, wooden furniture and furnishings of a living room. The assessor watches your safety, method, choice of products and finish.

blocks.note: Use a floor machine only as you have been trained, with your instructor watching. In practical work, never stand on furniture, and never mix cleaning products.

ul: **Gloves:** to protect your skin from detergent and chemicals.
**Goggles:** when you clean above head height with a chemical, or use strong products such as a stripper.
**Non-slip, closed shoes:** wet floors are slippery.
**Mask:** for dusty work, or as the product label says.
A wet-floor sign, though not PPE, is the most important safety item for floor work.

blocks.note: A floor cleaner has been poured into an unlabelled spray bottle. Do not use it. A person who does not know what is inside might swallow it, mix it with something else or use it on the wrong surface. Report it to your supervisor so it can be removed or labelled.
blocks.label: Safety

blocks.p: The **pH scale** runs from 0 to 14. **7 is neutral**. Below 7 is acid; above 7 is alkaline (alkali). Different dirt needs different types of cleaner, and different surfaces can be damaged by the wrong type.

head: Type
pH
Uses
Take care
rows: Neutral detergent (general cleaner)
About 7
Daily cleaning of most floors, walls and furniture; gentle and safe on most surfaces.
Measure it; too much leaves a sticky film.
Acid cleaner (descaler)
Below 7
Lime scale on taps, shower glass and ceramic tile in bathrooms.
Never on marble, terrazzo or limestone; it etches them. Never mix with bleach.
Alkaline cleaner or degreaser
Above 7
Heavy grease in kitchens; floor strippers are strongly alkaline.
Can damage wood, aluminium and some floors; wear gloves and goggles; rinse well.
Glass cleaner
Usually mild alkaline
Glass, mirrors and some shiny surfaces.
Spray on the cloth, not on the surface.
Furniture polish
Various
Wooden furniture; a little gives shine and protection.
Too much builds up a sticky film that holds dust.
Disinfectant
Various
Kills germs on clean surfaces such as door handles and bathrooms.
Clean first; use for the contact time on the label.
Abrasive cleaner (cream or powder)
Alkaline
Stubborn marks on tough surfaces.
Can scratch glass, plastic, chrome and polished stone. Do not use unless the surface allows.

blocks.p: Use a **neutral cleaner** for daily cleaning of most floors and furniture, because it is gentle and does not harm most surfaces. Move to a stronger product only when you must, and only on a surface that can take it.

head: Tool
Use
rows: Dust mop (wide, flat, used dry)
Collects dust and grit from hard floors.
Broom and dustpan
Loose dirt on rough floors, terraces and corners.
Damp mop or string mop, two buckets
Washing floors; one bucket for the cleaner, one for clean rinse water.
Wringer
Wrings out a mop so it leaves the floor only slightly damp.
Floor squeegee (long rubber edge)
Pushes water across a floor towards a drain.
Rotary floor machine with pads or brushes
Scrubs, strips or polishes large floors.
Wet-and-dry vacuum
Picks up dirty water after scrubbing.
Long-handled cobweb brush and fan duster
Reaching high corners and fan blades from the floor.
Stepladder
Reaching high places when long tools are not enough.
Microfibre cloths
Dusting, wiping glass and mirrors without lint.
Sponges, scouring pads (non-scratch)
Washing walls and tiles; test on a hidden spot.
Colour-coded cloths and buckets
Stop germs spreading: for example red for toilets and a different colour for other surfaces, as the property's colour code says.

blocks.note: Microfibre cloths pick up dust and grease with very fine fibres. Wash them without fabric softener, because softener coats the fibres and they stop working.
blocks.label: Tip

sections.title: Planning and surfaces: know what you are cleaning

blocks.p: Before you clean a room, walk round and look at each surface. Find out what it is made of, what dirt is on it and whether anything is already damaged. Then choose the product and method. **Some cleaners and methods damage some surfaces.**

flow: Walk round the room and look
Note the surfaces, dirt and damage
Choose products and tools
Test on a hidden spot if unsure
Clean from high to low, dry before wet
Check and report

head: Floor
What it is
Cleaning
Do not
rows: Marble
Polished natural stone; soft and easily etched.
Dust mop daily; damp mop with a neutral cleaner made for stone; wipe spills fast.
Never use acid cleaners, vinegar or lime juice; they etch dull marks. Do not use abrasive pads or too much water.
Terrazzo
Marble chips set in cement and ground smooth; common in older Jamaican homes.
Neutral cleaner; polish with a machine and the right pad to restore shine.
No acid cleaners; no heavy scrubbing that dulls the surface.
Ceramic tile
Fired clay tile with a glaze; common in kitchens and bathrooms.
Neutral cleaner; scrub the grout with a brush; acid descaler is allowed on glazed tile for lime scale if the label says so.
Do not leave cleaner behind; it makes tile slippery.
Vinyl
A flexible plastic floor, often polished with a floor finish.
Dust mop, damp mop; spray buff or strip and refinish when needed.
No solvents; avoid too much water at the seams.
Wood and laminate
Boards or planks; wood can be sealed or waxed; laminate is a thin layer over fibreboard.
Dust mop; a barely damp mop; dry at once.
Too much water soaks in, so boards swell, lift or stain. No steam mops.
Concrete and cement
Rough, hard-wearing; found on terraces and outdoor areas.
Sweep; scrub with a stiff brush and detergent; rinse.
Do not use machine pads meant for polish.
Carpet and rugs
Fibre floor covering.
Vacuum; treat spills quickly by blotting; follow the maker's advice.
Do not rub a spill; it spreads and pushes the stain in.

blocks.note: Jamaican floors take a beating from sand, grit and salt carried in on shoes. Grit under shoes scratches tile, marble and wood and dulls the surface. Sweep or dust mop every day, and use barrier mats at doors so most of the grit stays outside.
blocks.label: Jamaica

ul: **Painted walls:** most are emulsion paint and can be washed gently, but flat or old paint may come off. Always test the cleaner in a hidden spot first.
**Tiled walls:** neutral cleaner; scrub grout lines; rinse and dry to prevent water spots.
**Wallpaper, wood panelling, fabric-covered walls:** dust only, or follow the supervisor's instructions.
**Ceilings:** dust with a long-handled tool; wash only if painted and marked washable.

head: Item
Material
How to care for it
rows: Tables, dressers, bed heads
Polished wood
Dust daily with a soft cloth; damp dust if needed; polish sparingly.
Patio furniture
Metal, plastic, wicker or cane
Wipe with mild detergent and fresh water; dry; sea salt rusts metal quickly.
Sofas and chairs
Fabric or leather
Vacuum with the upholstery tool; blot spills; follow the maker's care label.
Mirrors, glass table tops, picture glass
Glass
Clean glass with a cloth lightly sprayed with glass cleaner, then polish dry with a clean microfibre cloth.
Lampshades
Fabric or paper
Dust with a soft brush or the vacuum's brush tool; never wet.
Blinds
Wood, plastic or metal slats
Close the slats, then dust or wipe from top to bottom.
Curtains
Fabric
Vacuum or shake; send to the laundry as the property's schedule says.
Ceiling fans
Metal or wood blades
Switch off and wait for the fan to stop; wipe each blade with a damp cloth so dust does not fall.
Taps, towel rails, door handles
Chrome or brass
Mild cleaner, then dry and buff with a dry cloth.

blocks.h: Dust mopping or sweeping: always first

blocks.p: The first step in cleaning a hard floor is to **remove loose dust and grit** with a dust mop or broom. If you start with water, grit turns into mud and is rubbed across the floor like sandpaper.

ul: Use a clean, dry dust mop; keep it on the floor and push it along without lifting.
Work from the far side towards the door, pulling the dust into a line; then pick it up with a dustpan.
Move small furniture, rugs and bins out of the way, and sweep under and behind furniture.
Do not shake the mop out inside the room.

flow: Collect a mop, two buckets, a neutral cleaner, a measuring jug, gloves and wet floor signs
Move furniture and rugs; sweep or dust mop the floor
Put clean water in the rinse bucket; measure the cleaner as the label says into the cleaning bucket
Put out wet floor signs
Dip the mop in the cleaning bucket and wring it out well, so it is damp, not dripping
Mop in sections, working back towards the door so you do not walk on the clean floor; use a figure-of-eight or side-to-side pattern
Rinse the mop often in the rinse bucket, wring it, and change the water when it is dirty
Mop the edges and corners; let the floor dry; remove signs only when dry
Empty and rinse buckets and mops, and hang the mop to dry

head: Question
Answer
rows: What is a damp mop?
A mop wrung out well, so it leaves the floor only slightly wet.
Why two buckets?
One has the cleaning solution; the other has rinse water to wash dirt out of the mop. A single bucket just spreads dirty water.
Why do I rinse after scrubbing a tiled floor?
To remove cleaner left behind that can make the floor slippery and attract dirt.
Why measure the cleaner?
Too strong leaves a film or damages the surface; too weak does not clean.
Why work back towards the door?
So you do not walk across the wet floor you have just cleaned.

blocks.note: A wet floor is a slip hazard. Use signs and close the area. If you must leave a wet floor, stay near it or block it until it is dry. Never leave a wet floor in a guest corridor without signs.
blocks.label: Safety

ul: Wipe up spills at once, before they soak in, especially on marble, wood and carpet.
On marble, fruit juice, wine and rum punch can leave stains or etch marks. Blot with a damp cloth, rinse and dry; if a mark remains, report it so it can be treated.
On carpet, blot from the edge towards the centre; do not rub.
Put out a sign after wiping, until the floor is dry.

head: Situation
What to do
rows: Grout lines in a bathroom floor
Scrub with a stiff brush and neutral or suitable cleaner; rinse and dry.
Salt and sand at a villa entrance
Barrier mat; sweep daily; mop after sweeping.
Sticky patch from spilled drink
Warm water and neutral cleaner; rinse so no film remains.
Dull terrazzo even after mopping
Polish with a floor machine and the right pad; a film of old cleaner may need removing first.

blocks.p: A **rotary floor machine** spins a pad or brush under it to scrub, strip or polish a floor. It does the work of many hours of hand scrubbing, but it is powerful and can run away from you, damage a floor or cause shocks. Use it only after training and with your supervisor's permission.

head: Pad colour (common code)
Typical job
rows: White or light
Polishing, light buffing.
Red
Spray buffing; light cleaning.
Blue or green
Scrubbing; cleaning heavier dirt.
Brown or black (dark)
Stripping old floor finish.
Brush (bristle)
Scrubbing tile and grout, concrete and terraces.

blocks.p: In general, **darker pads scrub harder; lighter pads polish**. Colours differ between makers, so always check the maker's chart.

ul: Read the maker's instructions and use only the pad and settings it allows.
Check the plug, cable and body for cuts, burns and loose parts. Do not use a damaged machine; report it.
With the machine **unplugged**, check the pad is in good condition and fitted correctly, centred and locked.
Clear the area, put out signs and keep guests away.
Wear non-slip shoes, and gloves and eye protection if using chemicals.

flow: Plug in near the area and keep the cable **behind you, over your shoulder, away from the pad**
Hold the handle with both hands, feet apart
Start with the machine tilted so the pad is off the floor, then lower it gently
Walk slowly and steadily, moving the machine in overlapping passes, side to side
Do not let it stay in one place; this wears the floor and may burn the pad
Keep an eye on the cable and the people around you
When finished, tilt the machine up, switch off, wait for the pad to stop and unplug it

blocks.note: To change a pad, switch off and **unplug the machine first**. A machine that starts by accident can cut you badly.
blocks.label: Safety

flow: Look at the floor, find out what it is made of, plan the job
Clear furniture, put out signs and close off the area
Check the machine, plug, cable and pad with the machine unplugged
Sweep or dust mop
Mix the cleaner as the label says; spread it on a section; scrub in sections with the right pad
Pick up the dirty water with a wet-and-dry vacuum or mop; rinse with clean water
When the floor is dry, buff with a polishing pad if the floor and the Centre's rules allow
Check the floor; put furniture back; clean, dry and store the machine, pad off, cable coiled

head: Machine problem
Cause
Cure
rows: Machine pulls to one side
Pad worn unevenly or fitted off-centre; too much pressure
Switch off; refit or replace the pad; lighten your hold.
Machine jerks or jumps
Debris under the pad; pad too aggressive for the floor
Switch off; clean the pad; use a gentler pad.
White haze on the floor
Cleaner not rinsed off
Rinse with clean water and pick up.
Swirl marks
Dirty or hard pad on a soft floor
Use a clean, softer pad.
Machine stops
Tripped cable, blown fuse or overloaded plug
Unplug; check the cable; ask for help.

blocks.p: Unplug the machine, clean it, remove the pad and wash it, and store the machine and pad dry. Coil the cable loosely, not tightly around the handle. A damp pad left on the machine will smell and wear out fast.

sections.title: Stripping and refinishing a vinyl floor

blocks.p: **Stripping** means removing old floor polish (finish) with a strong chemical and a machine. Floor finish builds up over time, yellows, and wears in patches. When a floor looks dull and dirty after cleaning, it is time to strip and refinish.
Do it when the area can be closed for some hours: between bookings, or at a quiet time. A large villa's floors are best done when it is empty.

flow: Put out signs; close the area; remove furniture; sweep the floor
Put on gloves, eye protection and non-slip shoes
Mix the stripper exactly as the label says
Spread it on a small section with a mop; leave it for the time on the label, without letting it dry
Scrub with a dark (stripping) pad on the floor machine
Pick up the slurry (the dirty stripper and old finish) with the wet-and-dry vacuum
Rinse the floor twice with clean water; pick up the rinse water; let the floor dry fully
Check there is no old finish or white haze left
Apply thin coats of new floor finish with a clean mop or applicator; let each coat dry before the next
Keep the area closed until the finish is dry and hard, as the label says

blocks.note: Stripper is a strong alkaline chemical and the floor becomes very slippery. Wear gloves, goggles and non-slip shoes. Never walk across a stripped floor in street shoes. Stripper left on the floor stops the new finish from sticking.
blocks.label: Safety

ul: After stripping a vinyl floor, **new coats of finish** are put on and left to dry before the room is used again.
Do not mix the stripper with other chemicals.
Work in small sections so the stripper does not dry on the floor.

blocks.h: Order of work: top to bottom, dry before wet

blocks.p: Dust and dirt fall down. Always clean **from the top** (cobwebs, ceiling corners, light fittings, fans) **down** to the walls, furniture, and floor last. Do dry work (dusting, vacuuming) before wet work (washing).

blocks.h: Removing cobwebs and dust from high places

ul: Use a long-handled cobweb brush or duster from the floor, not a ladder, where you can.
Start in the corners and move along the top of the wall.
Roll the web onto the brush instead of smearing it.
Check light fittings, curtain tops, picture rails and the tops of cupboards.

flow: Dust the wall first with a dry cloth or long-handled duster
Protect the floor and furniture with a dust sheet; keep water away from sockets and switches
Mix a mild detergent in warm water as the label says; put clean water in a second bucket
Test the solution on a small hidden spot to check the paint does not come off or mark
Wearing gloves, wash with a sponge or cloth wrung out well, from the bottom up, so that drips do not run down over dry paint and leave streaks
Rinse with a clean cloth and clean water
Dry with a clean cloth, and check for streaks or tide marks

blocks.note: The common advice is to wash walls from the bottom up, so that drips do not run down dirt and leave streaks that are hard to remove. Always dry and rinse each section before moving on. If your property or the Centre uses a different method, follow it.
blocks.label: Tip

head: Problem
How to deal with it
rows: Scuff marks on paint
Rub gently with a damp cloth and a little mild cleaner; do not scrub, as it removes paint.
Crayon, pen or grease
Mild cleaner on a cloth; test first; report if it will not come off.
Finger marks round switches and door frames
Damp cloth with mild detergent; keep water away from the switch.
Black spots on a bathroom ceiling
Probably mould: see below.
Peeling paint, cracks, damp patches
Do not clean; report to supervisor or maintenance.

blocks.p: In Jamaica's warm, damp weather, **mould** grows in damp, poorly aired places such as bathroom ceilings, grout, the backs of cupboards and under leaking pipes. It appears as black, green or grey spots and smells musty.

ul: Wear gloves, goggles and a mask if the product says so. Air the room.
Use the right mould product as the label says, and do not mix it with other chemicals.
Do not dry-brush mould, which sends spores into the air.
**Report it.** Mould keeps coming back until the cause is found: a leak, poor airflow or no extractor fan.

ol: Can you do the job from the floor with a long-handled tool? That is safest.
If you need a stepladder, check it first: legs, steps, feet and locking bars must be sound; nothing bent or missing.
Set it **fully open** on firm, level, dry ground, with the spreader locked. Clear the area round it.
Wear non-slip shoes. Climb facing the ladder, keeping **three points of contact**: two feet and one hand, or two hands and one foot.
Keep your hips between the sides of the ladder. Do not lean or stretch to the side: **come down and move the ladder**.
Never stand on the top step or on a chair, table or bed.
Carry cloths and products in a belt or small bucket on a hook, not in your hand while climbing.
Switch off fans and lights before you reach them; do not use a ladder near electric wires.

blocks.note: A ladder is not a place to rush. More cleaners are hurt falling from a stepladder than from any other cleaning job.
blocks.label: Safety

ul: Dust every day with a soft, clean cloth, or a damp-dust cloth wrung out well so it picks the dust up and does not spread it.
Never wet wood heavily, and dry it straight away. Water leaves marks and makes wood swell.
Clean sticky marks with a cloth barely damp with mild soapy water, then dry the spot.
Use furniture polish **sparingly**, on a cloth rather than sprayed on the wood, and rub with the grain. Too much polish builds up a sticky film that holds dust.
A white ring from a cold or hot glass is a mark in the finish: wipe it dry and **report it** so it can be treated properly. Do not scrub it or use abrasive products.

blocks.p: Smears come from a dirty cloth, or too much cleaner left on the glass. For a streak-free finish:

flow: Dust the frame and glass with a dry cloth
Spray glass cleaner onto a cloth, not onto the glass
Wipe in an S-shape or in straight lines
Polish dry with a clean, dry, lint-free or microfibre cloth
Check from the side for smears

ul: For a framed picture with glass in front, spray the cleaner onto the cloth, then wipe the glass; liquid running behind the glass will mark the picture.
A crack in a glass table top is dangerous. Take it out of use if you can, and report it.
Chrome taps and towel rails: mild cleaner, then dry with a dry cloth so they shine and do not mark with water.
Metal patio furniture by the sea goes rusty quickly because **salt in the sea air** speeds up rust. Wipe off salt with fresh water, dry it and report any rust.
Never use steel wool on chrome or stainless steel.

head: Item
Safe method
rows: Table lamp
Switch off; unplug where you can; let the bulb cool; dust the shade with a soft brush; wipe the base with a damp cloth, keeping water away from the wiring.
Ceiling fan
Switch off and wait for it to stop; use a long-handled fan duster or a checked stepladder; wipe each blade with a damp cloth so dust falls into the cloth.
Blinds
Close the slats and dust or wipe from top to bottom; turn them over and do the other side.
Curtains
Vacuum with a soft brush; shake gently; report stains or damage.
Upholstery
Vacuum with the upholstery tool; blot spills with a damp cloth; follow the care label.
Cushions
Plump and arrange; report stains.

blocks.note: Never spray liquid on or near a switch, a plug or a lamp socket. Switch off at the wall, and unplug where you can, before you clean any electrical item.
blocks.label: Safety

head: Condition
Effect
What you do
rows: Sand and grit
Scratches tile, marble and wood; dulls shine.
Barrier mats; dust mop daily.
Salt air (seaside villas)
Rusts metal; leaves a film on glass and furniture.
Wipe metal and glass with fresh water, dry; report rust.
Heat and humidity
Mould and mildew; sticky surfaces; warping of wood.
Air rooms; keep surfaces dry; clean mould early.
Hard water (limestone water)
White, chalky lime marks on taps, glass and tiles.
Acid descaler where the surface allows, then rinse; never on marble or terrazzo.
Strong sun
Fades fabric, dries and cracks wood.
Close blinds; report fading and cracks.
Power and water cuts
Machines cannot be used; no water for rinsing.
Plan work; know the supervisor's contingency; do not start a job you cannot rinse.

blocks.p: When you finish, stand at the door and look at the room as a guest would.

ul: Look along the floor towards the light for streaks, dull patches, footprints and missed corners, and under and behind furniture.
Check walls for streaks or tide marks, and for cobwebs high up.
Run a clean hand or cloth over furniture tops, picture frames and skirting boards to check for dust.
Look at glass and mirrors from the side for smears.
Check that the furniture and furnishings are **put back in their usual places, straight and tidy**.
Check lights, fans and taps work and are switched off or on as required.
Collect your equipment: unplug, clean and store the machine; empty and rinse buckets; wash cloths; put products away and lock them.
Report cracks, chips, rust, loose fittings, damp patches, stains that will not come out and broken items to your supervisor or on a maintenance form.
Write down what, where, and when you found it. Take a photo only if the property allows.
Do not try to repair anything yourself, and do not move a damaged item to hide it.

terms: Dust mop
A wide, flat mop used dry to collect dust and grit.
Damp mop
A mop wrung out well so it leaves the floor slightly wet.
Neutral cleaner
A cleaner with pH 7; gentle on most surfaces.
Detergent
A cleaning product that lifts dirt and grease off surfaces.
Etching
Dull marks cut into stone such as marble by acid.
Rotary floor machine
A machine that spins a pad or brush to scrub or polish floors.
Pad
A round nylon disc fitted under a floor machine.
Buffing
Polishing a hard floor with a fast-spinning machine to bring up the shine.
Stripping
Removing old floor polish with a strong chemical and a machine.
Floor finish
The polish put on a vinyl floor to protect it and give shine.
Slurry
The wet mix of stripper and old finish that is picked up after scrubbing.
Wet-and-dry vacuum
A vacuum that can pick up water.
Squeegee
A tool with a long rubber edge for pushing water across a floor.
Terrazzo
A floor of marble chips set in cement and ground smooth.
Ceramic tile
A tile made of fired clay with a shiny glaze.
Microfibre
A cloth with very fine fibres that cleans glass without lint.
Damp dusting
Dusting with a cloth that is slightly wet and well wrung out.
Mould
A fungus that grows in damp, poorly aired places.
Stepladder
A ladder that stands on its own legs.
Three points of contact
Always keeping two feet and one hand, or two hands and one foot, on the ladder.
PPE
Personal protective equipment: gloves, goggles, non-slip shoes and a mask.
SDS
Safety data sheet: gives safety information about a chemical.

c1.title: A marble floor at a villa in Ocho Rios
c1.text: Trainee Janelle is cleaning the polished marble floor in the living room of a villa in Ocho Rios. A bucket of lime juice and vinegar that a cook used to clean the kitchen is on the veranda. A guest has spilled a rum punch near the sofa and a sticky patch is spreading. The floor was swept yesterday but a lot of sand has blown in from the beach.

c2.title: A floor machine in a Mandeville guest house
c2.text: Trainee Rushane has permission to polish the terrazzo floor in a Mandeville guest house lounge. As he unrolls the cable, he sees a cut in the outer covering near the plug. The area has two guests' bags in it and a wet patch from a leaking plant pot. He has two pads on the trolley, one white and one black.

c3.title: Black spots in a Treasure Beach bathroom
c3.text: In a seaside villa at Treasure Beach, room attendant Marlon sees black spots on the bathroom ceiling and a musty smell. The window is small and there is no extractor fan. The same spots come back every few weeks, however often they are wiped. A guest says she is allergic to dust.

c4.title: A ceiling fan and a high cobweb in Negril
c4.text: Trainee Sasha must clean the ceiling fan and the cobwebs in the high corner of a bedroom in a Negril villa. The only ladder available is a stepladder with one bent foot. There is also a wooden table lamp beside the bed with a fabric shade.

c5.title: A wooden table in a villa living room in Port Antonio
c5.text: In a Port Antonio villa, a mahogany side table has a thin film of sticky polish and a white ring where a cold glass stood. The room also has a glass table top, a framed picture and a metal patio chair on the veranda that has rust spots. Trainee Odane is cleaning them.

c6.title: A corridor in a Kingston hotel
c6.text: The vinyl corridor floor on the second floor of a Kingston hotel is yellow and patchy, even after mopping. The hotel is full except on Tuesday afternoon, when most rooms on that floor are empty. Supervisor Mrs. Walker asks trainee Dane to strip and refinish it. He finds that the stripper bottle has a faded label and no safety data sheet nearby.

questions.q: What should Janelle do first about the rum punch spill on the marble floor?
o: Pour the lime juice mix on it to cut the sugar in the drink
Leave it to dry and sweep it up later in the day
Blot it up at once, then damp mop with a neutral stone cleaner
Scrub it hard with an abrasive powder and a stiff scrubbing brush
questions.why: Fruit and sugary drinks stain marble if left, so wipe up quickly with a damp cloth and clean with a neutral cleaner. Acid and abrasives would etch and scratch the stone.

questions.q: Why is the sand blown in from the beach a problem for the marble floor?
o: It scratches and dulls the floor when people walk on it
It makes the marble heavy and very hard to clean properly
It turns the marble yellow after only a few days on the floor
It reacts with the polish and makes the floor sticky to walk on
questions.why: Grit under shoes acts like sandpaper on a polished floor. Sweeping or dust mopping every day, and barrier mats at the doors, protect it.

questions.q: How should Janelle clean the whole marble floor today?
o: Dust mop first, then damp mop with a neutral stone cleaner
Flood it with water and a strong acid cleaner to remove the grit
Scrub it with a hard brush and powder for a deeper clean overall
Mop it with the kitchen's lime and vinegar mix to make it shine
questions.why: Marble is soft stone. Remove grit first, then clean damply with a neutral stone cleaner. Acid, abrasives and lots of water all damage it.

questions.q: Rushane sees a cut in the cable near the plug. What should he do?
o: Wrap it with tape and carry on, as the cut is small
Keep the cable away from the wet patch and use the machine
Use it only on the dry side of the lounge
Not use the machine, and report the damaged cable
questions.why: A damaged cable can cause an electric shock or fire, especially near water. Never use a damaged machine; report it so it is repaired or replaced.

questions.q: Which pad should Rushane use to polish the terrazzo?
o: The black pad, as it makes the floor shine faster and better
The white pad, as lighter pads polish and darker pads scrub
Either pad will do, as the colours make no difference at all
No pad is needed; the brush on its own is enough to polish it
questions.why: In the usual colour code lighter pads polish and darker pads scrub or strip, and a dark pad would scratch and dull terrazzo. Always check the maker's chart.

questions.q: Before he switches the machine on, what else must Rushane do about the area?
o: Pile the guests' bags in the middle of the floor to protect them
Clear it, put out signs and keep guests away
Switch on a fan to dry the plant pot's wet patch faster
Lock the lounge doors to stop the guests coming in
questions.why: Clear the area, put out signs and keep people away, and deal with the wet patch first. Locking guests out or leaving bags in the way are not safe or professional.

questions.q: Which conditions in Marlon's bathroom best explain why the spots keep coming back?
o: Hot sun and strong winds drying the ceiling too quickly
Damp air and no extractor fan or airflow to dry it out
Too much light from the window, which fades the paint
Dust from the beach settling on the ceiling each day
questions.why: Mould needs damp and still air. A small window, no extractor fan and steamy showers keep the ceiling damp, so the spots return unless the cause is fixed.

questions.q: Marlon wipes the spots away, but they come back. What is the best action?
o: Use a much stronger cleaner on the ceiling every week from now on
Clean it with the right product and PPE, and report the damp
Paint over the black spots with a fresh coat of white paint
Tell the guest to keep the bathroom window shut at all times
questions.why: Mould keeps coming back until the cause (a leak, no airflow) is fixed, so cleaning must be followed by a report to the supervisor or maintenance.

questions.q: Which is the safest way for Marlon to clean the mould?
o: Dry-brush it quickly and sweep up the dust that falls down
Mix bleach with an acid toilet cleaner for a stronger effect on it
Spray it with perfume so that the musty smell cannot be noticed
Wear gloves, goggles and a mask, air the room and follow the label
questions.why: Mould spores can irritate the lungs, so wear PPE and air the room. Dry brushing spreads spores, and mixing bleach with acid gives off a poisonous gas.

questions.q: What should Sasha do about the stepladder with a bent foot?
o: Use it carefully, with a colleague holding it steady for her
Put a book under the bent foot to make the ladder level
Not use it, and report it or ask for another ladder
Use it only for the low corner of the room, not the high one
questions.why: A ladder with a bent or missing part is unsafe and must be taken out of use. Check every ladder before climbing.

questions.q: Sasha has a good ladder. How should she work on it?
o: Stand on the top step so that she can reach further across the fan
Keep three points of contact, and move the ladder, not stretch
Carry the bucket of cleaner in one hand and climb with the other hand
Lean the ladder against the wall so that it is steadier to climb on
questions.why: A stepladder stands on its own, fully open, on firm ground. Keep three points of contact, keep your hips between the sides and come down to move it. Never stand on the top step.

questions.q: What must Sasha do before she cleans the table lamp?
o: Spray the shade with water to wash off the dust
Switch it off, and unplug it if she can
Take the bulb out with a wet cloth to cool it
Leave it plugged in so she can test it afterwards
questions.why: Always switch off and unplug electrical items before cleaning. Fabric shades are dusted with a soft brush, never wetted, and water is kept away from the wiring.

questions.q: What is the best way to deal with the sticky film on the mahogany table?
o: Use a cloth barely damp with mild soapy water, then dry it
Spray on more polish to dissolve the old layer that is on there
Wash it with a wet sponge and leave it to dry in the sun
Rub it with a scouring pad and an abrasive cleaner until it is clean
questions.why: Heavy polish builds up into a sticky film, so remove it with a barely damp cloth and mild soapy water and dry the wood at once. Too much water or abrasives damage wood.

questions.q: Odane finds a white ring on the table top. What should he do?
o: Rub it hard with the scouring pad until it goes
Leave it, as nobody will notice it in the living room
Cover it with a mat so the guests do not see it
Wipe the area dry and report it for proper treatment
questions.why: A white ring is a mark in the finish. Scrubbing could cause more damage. Dry the area and report it so it can be treated properly.

questions.q: How should Odane clean the glass table top for a streak-free finish?
o: Pour cleaner onto the glass and wipe it with a wet cloth afterwards
Spray cleaner on a cloth, wipe, then polish dry with microfibre
Wipe the glass with a dry paper towel only and nothing else at all
Wash it with a sponge and detergent and let it dry in the open air
questions.why: Smears come from a dirty cloth or too much cleaner. A lightly sprayed cloth and a clean, dry, lint-free cloth for polishing leave glass clear.

questions.q: Why does the metal patio chair rust so quickly at a seaside villa?
o: Because patio chairs are made of very cheap metal
Because the guests use them in the rain
Because salt in the sea air speeds up rust
Because chairs are never dried after cleaning
questions.why: Salt in the air settles on metal and speeds up rusting. Wipe off the salt with fresh water, dry the chair, and report rust so it can be treated.

questions.q: When is the best time to strip and refinish the corridor floor?
o: Tuesday afternoon, when most rooms on that floor are empty
Saturday night, when most of the guests are out for the evening
Straight away, while the guests walk carefully round the signs
During breakfast, so that the floor will be dry before lunch time
questions.why: Stripping needs the area closed for some hours, and the floor is slippery and chemical-wet. Plan it for a quiet time when it will not disturb or endanger guests.

questions.q: The stripper bottle has a faded label and no safety data sheet nearby. What should Dane do?
o: Use it, as floor stripper always has the same strength in every bottle
Mix it with water until it smells a lot weaker than before
Pour it into a new bottle and put a new label on it himself
Not use it until he has the label and SDS; ask the supervisor
questions.why: Never use a chemical you cannot identify. The label and SDS tell you how to mix it, what PPE to wear and what to do in an emergency.

questions.q: After scrubbing with stripper, what must Dane do before applying new finish?
o: Pick up the slurry, rinse twice and let the floor dry fully
Apply the new finish straight away over the wet stripper on the floor
Mop it once more with the stripper to help the new finish stick to it
Sweep it with a dry broom to remove all of the dirt and slurry
questions.why: Stripper left on the floor stops the new finish from sticking and can cause a haze. The slurry is picked up, the floor is rinsed and left to dry, then thin coats of finish go on.

questions.q: A housekeeper cleans a painted wall from the top and finds that the paint is coming off on her cloth. What was the most likely mistake?
o: She used a cloth that was far too clean for the job
She did not test the cleaner on a hidden spot first
She worked from the floor up to the ceiling on the wall
She wore gloves all the time while she was working there
questions.why: Paint can be damaged by cleaner or by rubbing. A test on a small, hidden spot shows whether the wall will take the product before the whole wall is washed.
